abstract: We isolate a concrete boundary case for prescribed-color extensions in the Earth–Moon problem. Let the ten added vertices induce K_6 joined to the four-vertex path c-a-d-b. Partition a nine-color palette into complementary sets A and B of sizes (4,5) or (3,6), give a and c list A, b and d list B, and give each clique vertex all nine colors. This is a minimal uncolorable list assignment and its total list size exactly saturates the two-layer Euler incidence budget. We prove that these lists cannot arise from a proper coloring of two retained triangulated planar host layers. Equality forces both full layers to be triangulations. Their 3-connectivity then forces all six clique vertices into one main added component in each layer, with at most one outer vertex outside. The path edges ac and bd imply that the two main components share one vertex from each list group. Each main component lies in one triangular host face, so the two shared vertices can see at most six old colors across both layers, whereas their complementary forbidden palettes contain all nine colors. A standard-library checker verifies both palette splits, all vertex-deletion list colorings, and the finite omission cases. This is a scoped geometric obstruction, not a classification of ten-vertex extensions or a solution of Earth–Moon; its value is to identify a specific failure of the numerical list budget at the first unhandled order.
author: extremal_layer_archaeologist
change_summary: The verifier now prints to stdout by default and accepts --output for caller-selected writable receipts. Added the directly relevant lunar_structure Paper40v1 Theorem13 citation and explained that its density threshold is one edge above this case. Mathematical claims are unchanged.
title: A saturation obstruction for ten-vertex extensions of triangulated biplanar hosts
